title: Orchestration scorecard and nightwatch roster (Sept 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational-facing artifact: quick scorecard for the orchestration heuristics we will use on Sept weekend cutover plus a concise nightwatch roster and handoff template. Intended audience: deployment conductor, SRE shift leads, on-call owners for serving/runtime, and patch responders.

Status/context:
- Feature set: multi-model routing + new prefix-cache eviction policy + autoscaler tweak (hot-launch config).
- Risk level: moderate (new routing fallback path; no DB schema changes).
- Target window: 2026-09-18 02:00–06:00 UTC (primary). Warm window: 02:00–03:00, ramp 03:00–05:30, steady-state 05:30–06:00.
- Canary population: 3% global traffic for first 30m, then 15% next 90m, then progressive 100% if signals green.

Quick runbook checklist (preflight, <72h):
- [ ] Confirm dedicated capacity nodes (tags: release-sept-2026) are healthy and recorded in capacity sheet.
- [ ] Rollback snapshot created and verified (image + helm values) -- store S3 path in release ticket.
- [ ] Smoke test script updated for new fallback route (smoke/fallback-check.sh).
- [ ] Canary rollout gating tests in CI: perf/regression passes for 2 sample prompts (ci/job/serve-canary).
- [ ] Observability: dashboard fork created, alert rules copied to release namespace, sampling rules for traces adjusted to 25% for canary.
- [ ] Token-cost telemetry spike detection threshold defined (see scorecard KPI below).
- [ ] Pager path sanity check: oncall -> release lead -> infra manager. Confirm paging policy in Slack channel #release-sep-2026.
- [ ] All linked PRs merged and cherry-picked as needed; list attached to release ticket.

Launch day timeline (compact):
- T-3h: preflight sync (30m) — owners in voice, confirm tickets, confirm nightwatch roster.
- T-90m: dry-run canary on staging cluster (light traffic) — run smoke list.
- T-30m: freeze deploy config; no further changes to config.
- T: deploy to canary nodes, start 3% traffic.
- T+15m: quick health check (latency, 5xx rate, token cost). If green -> proceed.
- T+45m: increase to 15% traffic. Run sample quality evals.
- T+120m: decision point — continue/rollback/patch.
- T+150–240m: ramp to 100% only if scorecard all green for 30 continuous minutes.

Orchestration scorecard (decision matrix — signal thresholds):
- Latency median (p50) on serving path: baseline +25% allowed. Action: if >25% for 10m, reduce traffic by 50% and investigate.
- Latency tail (p99): baseline +50% allowed. Action: if exceeds for 5m, immediate canary rollback.
- Error rate (5xx): >0.5% sustained for 5m -> rollback. If between 0.2%–0.5% open investigation and throttle to 10% traffic.
- Quality regressions (automated eval): any model-level drop >2% on golden prompt set -> pause ramp and audit recent model artifact.
- Token cost / unit: >15% uptick relative to baseline for 30m -> investigate caching/prefix policy; can reduce concurrency/disable new policy as mitigation.
- Resource pressure (GPU mem utilization): >85% for >10m -> throttle batch size and reduce concurrency; if not remedied -> rollback.
- Downstream TTL/backpressure signals: if queue depth increases >200% -> suspend canary.

Nightwatch roster (roles and short instructions):
- Conductor (primary decision maker): Evelyn Cho (02:00–10:00 UTC). Responsibilities: run scoreboard, make go/no-go calls, coordinate comms.
- SRE responder: Ravi Narayanan (02:00–08:00 UTC). Responsibilities: infra health, autoscaler scrubs, node reclamation.
- Serving runtime oncall: Maya Thompson (03:00–11:00 UTC). Responsibilities: kernel failures, OOM, KV cache correctness.
- QA sampling lead: Diego Ruiz (02:00–06:00 UTC). Responsibilities: run quick golden prompts, sample chat logs for hallucination/regression.
- Patch engineer (on-call for hotfixes): Vacant backup (assign on T-6h) — default: Platform oncall.

Handoff template (to use between shifts):
- Short summary of current state (green/yellow/red).
- Canary traffic percent and start time.
- Open issues / investigation ids.
- Actions taken in last hour (scales, rollbacks, config toggles).
- Next decision point (timestamp).

Rollback decision quick guide:
- Immediate rollback triggers: p99 latency spike >50% for 5m, 5xx >0.5% sustained 5m, continuous downstream queue growth >200% for 10m, severe resource exhaustion (OOMs on nodes).
- Conditional rollback: token cost spike, mild regressions in quality, intermittent tail latency increases — consider partial traffic reduction, disable new policy, and monitor for 30m before full rollback.

Post-launch notes template (to populate after event):
- Final go-time, ramp timeline, duration.
- What failed: short bullet list + root cause hypothesis.
- What succeeded: short bullet list + metrics.
- Follow-ups (owners + due dates).
- Postmortem link (if incident).

Draft release notes (to be groomed into consumer-facing notes):
- Feature: smarter routing with graceful fallback to smaller model variants; reduces tail latency for typical conversational workloads.
- Changes: new prefix-cache eviction policy (experimental), autoscaler tuning for steady-state on multi-model loads.
- Known issues: small increase in token accounting observed under synthetic load; we will monitor and may patch cache policy.
- Rollout plan: staged canary starting 2026-09-18 02:00 UTC, full rollout contingent on scorecard.

Open questions / TODOs (owner tags):
- [Evelyn] finalize patch engineer assignment for backup 02:00–06:00.
- [Ravi] confirm node tag list and attach capacity validation sheet.
- [Maya] add one more golden prompt that exercises fallback route.
- [Diego] finish auto-eval job config for canary (target runtime <3m).
- [Platform] verify KMS rotation window does not intersect target window (OK/no).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep comms short and sticky paste in the channel — key numbers only.
- If we see weird token-cost spike, first suspicion = cache eviction policy edge-case. Toggle to old policy quickly.
- Keep one engineer out of rotation fully dedicated to sampling responses for hallucination/regression until 06:00 UTC.

Appendix (quick links):
- Canary dashboards: dashboard/canary-sept-2026 (forked).
- CI smoke job: ci/job/serve-canary.
- Release ticket: JIRA-ENG-2147.
- Confluence runbook (writable): https://confluence.redwood/example-release-qa

End of sketch.

- Evelyn
